newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dead girl's sister urges calm as Belgium mourns.
newsitem.headline: Dead girl's sister urges calm as Belgium mourns.

text.p: The sister of a nine-year-old girl found dead in the basement of a Brussels garage called for calm on Friday as shocked Belgians went into mourning for the fifth young girl found dead in six months.

"You can destroy the whole earth, but she cannot come back," said Nabela Benaissa the day after Moroccan youths stoned the town hall in the Brussels suburb of Ixelles where the Benaissa family lives, and where her sister's body was found on Wednesday.
"Tomorrow must be the funeral, not a riot...In the name of Loubna let us say goodbye to her in peace," said Nabela, 17, who intervened to quell the disturbances on Thursday night.
The body of Loubna Benaissa, who disappeared in August 1992 while shopping for yoghurt for her mother, was discovered in a steel trunk in the basement of a Q8 garage in Ixelles.

Patrick Derochette, a convicted violent child molester who worked at the garage, was charged on Thursday with abduction, rape of a child under 10 years of age and illegal imprisonment leading to death.
Yves Crochelet, a psychiatrist who studied Derochette in 1984 when he was given a suspended sentence, described him on Friday as a "psychopathic pervert".

The funeral service, to be broadcast live to the nation, will take place at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT) on Saturday in Brussels Islamic Centre, after which Loubna's body will be flown to Tangiers, the family's place of origin, for burial on Sunday.
Hundreds of people are expected to attend the funeral service, and thousands are likely to line the streets to pay their last respects and show their support for the family.
Shock at the discovery of Loubna's body has turned to anger at the evident bungling by Brussels police in the first investigation.
On Friday Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene admitted that mistakes had been made.
"We cannot fail to take note of the fact that the Brussels inquiry failed. The Justice Minister will take the necessary measures," he told reporters.

"Key information neglected for four years," said the newspaper De Standaard. "Too many deficiencies: Anger covers the grief for Loubna," said Le Soir. "For four years, Loubna was just next door," wrote La Libre Belgique.

Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck admitted there had been serious flaws in the police investigations into Loubna's disappearance, and newspapers revealed that the garage had been searched at least three times in 1992 and 1996.
The discovery of Loubna's body brought to five the number of dead young girls found in Belgium since last August when another convicted paedophile, Marc Dutroux, was arrested.

Two young, sexually-abused girls were rescued from a dungeon in the basement of one of Dutroux' houses and the bodies of four girls were unearthed on two other properties either owned by or connected with him. Dutroux has been charged with murder.

There have been growing allegations of official protection for Dutroux, a theme that a special parliamentary commission has increasingly focused on since it began investigating bungled police investigations five months ago.
On Thursday the commission, which had been due to report on March 15, was given an extra month to pursue its inquiries.

Also on Thursday the parents of the other dead girls and of several other missing children visited the Benaissa family as did the members of the parliamentary commission. They are expected to attend the funeral on Saturday.
Police have not established any links between Dutroux and Derochette.
